name: Alpha
definition: The first letter of the Greek alphabet. In mathematics it commonly denotes an angle, a regression intercept, or a significance level in statistics, depending on context.

examples.explanation: Alpha names an angle of 30 degrees.

commonMistakes: Assuming alpha always means the same thing; its meaning is set by context.

name: Beta
definition: The second letter of the Greek alphabet. It commonly denotes a second angle, a regression coefficient in statistics, or a shape parameter of the beta distribution.

examples.explanation: Beta with subscripts names regression coefficients.

name: Gamma
definition: The third letter of the Greek alphabet. Lowercase gamma commonly denotes a curve parameter, a third angle, or the Euler-Mascheroni constant; uppercase Gamma denotes the gamma function.

examples.explanation: Gamma names a parametrized curve in the plane.

contexts.meaning: Uppercase Gamma is the gamma function, which extends the factorial.

name: Delta
definition: The fourth letter of the Greek alphabet. Lowercase delta commonly denotes a small quantity; uppercase Delta denotes a change, a discriminant, or a triangle, depending on context.

examples.explanation: Delta names a small positive quantity.

contexts.meaning: Uppercase Delta denotes a difference, as in Delta x.
An uppercase Delta can label a triangle.

name: Epsilon
definition: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, with the variant form ϵ. It most famously denotes an arbitrarily small positive quantity in limits and epsilon-delta arguments.

examples.explanation: For every positive epsilon, however small.

name: Zeta
definition: The sixth letter of the Greek alphabet. In mathematics it commonly denotes a complex variable or root, and names the Riemann zeta function.

examples.explanation: Zeta of 2 equals pi squared over 6.

examples.explanation: Lambda is the eigenvalue belonging to the eigenvector v.

name: Omicron
definition: The fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet. It looks identical to the Latin letter o, so it is rarely used as a mathematical symbol; big-O notation uses the Latin O instead.

examples.explanation: Big-O uses the Latin O, not omicron, for growth rates.

name: Pi
definition: The sixteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, with the variant form ϖ. Lowercase pi most famously denotes the circle constant; uppercase Pi denotes a product. Each meaning has its own entry.

examples.explanation: Pi is approximately 3.14159.

contexts.meaning: Lowercase pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
Uppercase Pi denotes a product of many factors.

examples.explanation: Rho names density: mass over volume.

name: Sigma
definition: The eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, with the word-final form ς. Lowercase sigma commonly denotes a standard deviation; uppercase Sigma denotes summation. Each use has its own entry.

examples.explanation: Sigma names a standard deviation of 2.

contexts.meaning: Lowercase sigma is the population standard deviation.
Uppercase Sigma denotes a sum of many terms.

name: Tau
definition: The nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet. It commonly denotes a time constant or a shear stress. Some writers propose tau, equal to two pi, as the circle constant; mainstream mathematics uses pi.

examples.explanation: In the tau proposal, one full turn is tau radians (about 6.283).

name: Upsilon
definition: The twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet. It is rarely used in mathematics; when it appears it is usually a generic variable. It is better known from physics, where it names a particle.

examples.explanation: Upsilon names an element of the set U.

commonMistakes: Confusing lowercase upsilon with the Latin letter u or with nu.

examples.explanation: Wave speed v equals frequency f times wavelength lambda.
